Availability

Read-only availability facts per provider: local model health, load, subscription quota and paid balance.

About 4 min read · 4 sections

On this page
01 What each provider row contains 02 Status rules 03 Collection 04 Settings

GET /v1/availability reports what this gateway can serve right now, so an agent or script can keep working when one account or server is used up or down. It reports facts only. Fixed model aliases do not switch providers because of these facts. Explicit managed worker routes consume the facts in their separate admission policy; callers opt into them by selecting a managed alias. The endpoint itself never mutates a route or reorders the catalog.

The endpoint needs the gateway client token, like every other non-health route. gateway availability [--json] [--wait MS] prints the same report for this Mac. It exits 0 whenever it prints a report. When the gateway cannot answer, it prints status: "unknown" with a fixed reason, so a caller can carry on as before.

What each provider row contains

Field Source Notes
status derived available, busy, unknown, limited or unavailable, with fixed reasons
load the provider's admission queue running, queued and limit on this Mac only
health local probe Only for self-hosted servers (loopback or tailnet: true)
quota Spendwatch or the gateway's own usage rows Windows, remainingPercent, account email
balance OpenRouter GET /credits Remaining and total USD
lastFailure, lastSuccessAt this gateway's request outcomes Fixed failure class and code only

Every observation carries observedAt and fresh. A source that fails keeps its last observation, which stops being fresh on its own; one failing source never removes the others.

Status rules

  • unavailable: a fresh probe says the local server is unhealthy, the last request failed with an authentication error within a day, or a connection failure within two minutes that no newer healthy probe has cleared.
  • limited: a live quota window is at 100% (until its reset, however old the reading), a quota failure within six hours with no later success or newer quota reading, a throttle until its Retry-After (two minutes without one), or a fresh zero balance.
  • unknown: a local server without a probe in the last 90 seconds.
  • busy: running requests reached the provider's limit, or requests are queued.
  • available: none of the above.

A later successful request clears every failure-based reason. Missing quota is not a reason: no data means no claim, never "has headroom".

Collection

Availability's health, quota and balance collection starts with the first request and stops after 30 minutes without one. Requests read the in-memory snapshot only. ?wait=MS (at most 5000) lets a cold request wait for the first round; the CLI waits 2500 ms by default. Opt-in admission capacity discovery separately refreshes inside the serving handler while its provider stays enabled, so queue limits can update before anyone requests an availability report.

Source Every Bound
Local probe, GET {baseUrl}/models per resolved address 20 s 3 s per address
Spendwatch capacity-current --provider codex|claude --json 2 min 15 s, 512 KiB
Account emails from the Codex credential record and Claude .claude.json 5 min read only
OpenRouter balance 5 min 5 s

A tailnet provider's probe uses the inference transport: the key is sent only to Tailscale addresses, and each address is checked separately, so one router down out of two reports degraded. Router-side load (running and waiting requests on the model servers) is not reachable from the Macs, so load covers this Mac's queue only.

With capacity discovery enabled, load.limit follows a fresh authenticated upstream slot count. Running and queued counts remain local to this Gateway. Discovery never interprets a slot count as free farm capacity, adds replicated router totals together, or rewrites configuration.

Settings

{ "availability": { "spendwatch": "/Users/me/.local/bin/spendwatch" } }

spendwatch is an absolute path. Without it, quota comes only from the gateway's own Codex usage counters and refused Claude windows. Spendwatch rows join a provider by the account email of its own local login; no credential or token is read into the report. The report contains no tokens, request bodies or file paths.
